          "content:encoded": "<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">Mandatory RBI Filings and Certifications for Companies with Non-Resident Shareholders</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>By CS Prashant Kumar</strong></p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\"><strong>Introduction: Why FEMA Compliance Matters from Day One</strong></h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>For Indian companies with foreign shareholders, incorporation is only half the work — the real scrutiny begins under&nbsp;<strong>FEMA (Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999)</strong>&nbsp;and India’s&nbsp;<strong>FDI (Foreign Direct Investment) Policy</strong>.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Whether your company has received FDI at incorporation or plans to raise funds later, it must comply with&nbsp;<strong>RBI reporting requirements</strong>&nbsp;and&nbsp;<strong>FEMA regulations</strong>. Missing these filings doesn’t just invite penalties — it can block future investment rounds, delay bank remittances, and raise red flags in due diligence.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:quote -->\n<blockquote class=\"wp-block-quote\"><!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>FEMA filings are not optional paperwork. They are your company’s official passport for foreign capital.—&nbsp;CS <em>Prashant Kumar</em></p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph --></blockquote>\n<!-- /wp:quote -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\"><strong>What Is FEMA Compliance and Why It’s Mandatory</strong></h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>FEMA compliance ensures that foreign investment received by an Indian company is legally reported to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) through filings like FC-GPR, FC-TRS, and FLA Return. These filings verify that the investment adheres to India’s FDI policy and sectoral caps.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>FEMA compliance applies whenever a&nbsp;<strong>non-resident</strong>&nbsp;invests in or transfers shares of an Indian company — whether at the time of incorporation or later.<br>It ensures that:</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>The inflow of funds is legally reported to RBI.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Sectoral caps and entry routes (automatic or approval) are followed.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>The company’s shareholding data matches RBI and MCA records.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\"><strong>Key FEMA Filings Every Company Must Know</strong></h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\"><strong>1. Form FC-GPR (Foreign Currency-Gross Provisional Return)</strong></h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>When shares are allotted to a&nbsp;<strong>non-resident investor</strong>, the company must file&nbsp;<strong>Form FC-GPR</strong>&nbsp;on the&nbsp;<strong>RBI FIRMS/Single Master Form (SMF)</strong>&nbsp;portal&nbsp;<strong>within 30 days of allotment</strong>.<br>This filing records:</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Details of the investor and remittance.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Amount and date of investment.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Valuation certificate from a Chartered Accountant.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Updated shareholding pattern post-allotment.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>It must also include:</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Board Resolution</strong>&nbsp;approving the allotment.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Declaration</strong>&nbsp;by the Company Secretary.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>KYC report</strong>&nbsp;from the investor’s bank (verified by the AD bank).</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Failure to file FC-GPR within the 30-day window can attract&nbsp;<strong>penalties under FEMA’s compounding rules</strong>, which can extend to&nbsp;<strong>three times the investment amount</strong>&nbsp;in severe cases.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\"><strong>2. Form FC-TRS (Transfer of Shares)</strong></h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>When shares are transferred between a&nbsp;<strong>resident and a non-resident</strong>, the company (or its AD Bank) must file&nbsp;<strong>Form FC-TRS</strong>&nbsp;within&nbsp;<strong>60 days of receipt of consideration</strong>.<br>This form records details of:</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Buyer and seller (resident/non-resident).</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Mode of transfer and price per share.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Bank certificate evidencing fund flow.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Even secondary transfers — such as between family-held companies or offshore parents — must be reported if they involve a non-resident party.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\"><strong>3. Annual FLA Return (Foreign Liabilities and Assets Return)</strong></h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Every Indian company that has received FDI or made overseas investment must file an&nbsp;<strong>Annual FLA Return</strong>&nbsp;with the&nbsp;<strong>RBI</strong>&nbsp;by&nbsp;<strong>15 July</strong>&nbsp;following the end of the financial year.<br>It captures:</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Foreign shareholding details.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Outstanding external liabilities.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Changes in foreign investment during the year.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>This return is filed online through the&nbsp;<strong>RBI FLAIR portal</strong>&nbsp;and applies even if there were&nbsp;<strong>no new transactions</strong>&nbsp;during the year.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:quote -->\n<blockquote class=\"wp-block-quote\"><!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>The FLA return is RBI’s annual census of India’s foreign investment ecosystem — missing it means falling off the regulator’s radar. —&nbsp;CS <em>Prashant Kumar</em></p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph --></blockquote>\n<!-- /wp:quote -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\"><strong>Professional Filings and Certificates Required</strong></h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Completing FEMA filings is a&nbsp;<strong>collaborative process</strong>&nbsp;involving multiple professionals and institutions:</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:table -->\n<figure class=\"wp-block-table\"><table class=\"has-fixed-layout\"><thead><tr><th><strong>Entity / Professional</strong></th><th><strong>Role in FEMA Compliance</strong></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><strong>Authorised Dealer (AD) Bank</strong></td><td>Handles inward remittance and verifies investor KYC.</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Chartered Accountant (CA)</strong></td><td>Issues valuation or pricing certificate for share allotment.</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Company Secretary (CS)</strong></td><td>Prepares Board resolutions, ensures consistency across MCA and RBI filings, and issues mandatory FEMA compliance certificate.</td></tr></tbody></table></figure>\n<!-- /wp:table -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\"><strong>Role of the Company Secretary’s Certificate (Now Mandatory)</strong></h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>A&nbsp;<strong>Company Secretary in practice</strong>&nbsp;must issue a certificate confirming that:</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Share allotment or transfer is duly authorised by the Board.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Shares are issued in compliance with the&nbsp;<strong>Companies Act, 2013</strong>&nbsp;and&nbsp;<strong>FEMA/FDI rules</strong>.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Statutory registers (<strong>MGT-1</strong>,&nbsp;<strong>SH-1</strong>) are updated and&nbsp;<strong>stamp duty</strong>&nbsp;has been paid.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Investor KYC and remittance details are verified.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>This certification, uploaded on the RBI FIRMS portal, assures the regulator that the company’s filings are consistent and compliant — reducing the risk of RBI queries or rejection.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:quote -->\n<blockquote class=\"wp-block-quote\"><!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>A FEMA certificate by a practising CS is not a formality — it’s your company’s shield against regulatory friction. —&nbsp;CS <em>Prashant Kumar</em></p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph --></blockquote>\n<!-- /wp:quote -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\"><strong>Common Mistakes to Avoid</strong></h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:list {\"ordered\":true} -->\n<ol class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Assuming small FDI doesn’t need reporting</strong>&nbsp;— even ₹1 received from a foreign shareholder requires FC-GPR filing.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Mismatch between MCA and RBI data</strong>&nbsp;— the number of shares and face value must match across platforms.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Missing the 30-day filing window</strong>&nbsp;— late filings require compounding, which can take months.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Ignoring FLA return</strong>&nbsp;— RBI actively tracks non-filers and issues reminders through AD banks.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Not coordinating with the AD bank</strong>&nbsp;— incorrect bank KYC or SWIFT copy can delay filing approvals.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ol>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\"><strong>Penalties for Non-Compliance</strong></h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Under&nbsp;<strong>Section 13 of FEMA</strong>, penalties include:</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Up to&nbsp;<strong>three times</strong>&nbsp;the amount involved in the contravention, or ₹2 lakh (whichever is higher).</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>₹5,000 per day for continuing default.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Possible compounding before RBI for delayed filings.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Beyond monetary penalties, FEMA non-compliance can&nbsp;<strong>delay further investment rounds</strong>,&nbsp;<strong>block dividend repatriation</strong>, and trigger queries during due diligence.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\"><strong>Best Practices for Smooth FEMA Compliance</strong></h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>File&nbsp;<strong>FC-GPR immediately after allotment</strong>&nbsp;— don’t wait till the 30-day deadline.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Maintain&nbsp;<strong>parallel data consistency</strong>&nbsp;between MCA filings (PAS-3) and RBI portal.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Keep&nbsp;<strong>KYC reports, FIRC copies, and Board Resolutions</strong>&nbsp;ready for upload.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Engage a&nbsp;<strong>CS in practice</strong>&nbsp;to certify the filing and handle coordination with the AD bank.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>File&nbsp;<strong>FLA return annually</strong>, even if there were no fresh transactions.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\"><strong>Summary: FDI Compliance Is Not Optional</strong></h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>FEMA and FDI compliance may look procedural, but they define your company’s credibility with both&nbsp;<strong>regulators and investors</strong>.<br>Every foreign-funded company in India — even with nominal FDI — must ensure timely FC-GPR, FC-TRS, and FLA filings with proper certification.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>In 2026, with <strong>AI-integrated data matching across MCA, RBI, and PAN systems</strong>, inconsistencies are instantly flagged.<br>Non-filing can freeze your company’s ability to raise funds, repatriate profits, or even remain compliant under Indian law.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:quote -->\n<blockquote class=\"wp-block-quote\"><!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>FEMA compliance is not about paperwork — it’s about proving your capital is clean, transparent, and compliant. —&nbsp;CS <em>Prashant Kumar</em></p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph --></blockquote>\n<!-- /wp:quote -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\"><strong>For More Clarity, See Our Related Articles</strong></h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul (2026 Guide)</a></strong><br>Complete timeline of post-registration filings and FEMA coordination.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong><a href=\"https://csatwork.in/form-inc-20a-filing-guide-india/\">Filing of Commencement of Business – Form INC-20A</a></strong><br>Learn why INC-20A approval is required before any FEMA filing.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong><a href=\"https://csatwork.in/issue-share-certificates-stamp-duty-india/\" data-type=\"link\" data-id=\"https://csatwork.in/issue-share-certificates-stamp-duty-india/\">Issue of Share Certificates &amp; Payment of Stamp Duty in India</a></strong><br>Ensure ownership proof and stamp duty payment before FEMA submissions.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Together, these guides form the&nbsp;<strong>Post-Incorporation Compliance Series by Pratham Legal</strong>&nbsp;— India’s most comprehensive resource for new companies navigating legal compliance.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator           "title": "Digital Nomad Visa India Explained: How Foreigners Can Legally Work Remotely in India (2026)",
          "link": "https://csatwork.in/digital-nomads-india-visa-tax-compliance/",
          "pubDate": "Sun, 09 Nov 2025 19:36:31 +0000",
          "dc:creator": "prashantmishra1986",
          "guid": {
            "#text": "https://csatwork.in/?p=31527",

              "isPermaLink": "false"

          "description": null,
          "content:encoded": "<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>India’s legal framework for remote-working foreigners explained — visas, taxation, FEMA rules, and compliance essentials (2026 Edition).</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>By CS Prashant Kumar</strong></p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">Introduction</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>India’s fast internet, cultural diversity, and affordable living make it an alluring destination for&nbsp;<strong>digital nomads</strong>&nbsp;— freelancers, remote employees, or entrepreneurs who work online while traveling. Yet, beneath the romantic idea of “coding from the beaches of Goa” or “consulting from a Rishikesh café” lies a serious legal question:</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>Can foreigners legally work online while living in India?</strong></p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Unlike Thailand, Indonesia, or Portugal,&nbsp;<strong>India does not have a formal “Digital Nomad Visa”</strong>. That absence creates a complex intersection between&nbsp;<strong>immigration law</strong>,&nbsp;<strong>tax residency</strong>, and&nbsp;<strong>foreign exchange regulations (FEMA)</strong>. A digital nomad may easily breach these unintentionally — simply by staying too long, earning locally, or using the wrong visa.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>This article explains what is&nbsp;<em>actually permitted</em>&nbsp;under Indian law and what remote workers must avoid to remain compliant.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\"><strong>Can foreigners legally work online from India?</strong></h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Foreigners can live in India and work online for overseas employers if their income comes exclusively from abroad. However, they cannot work for or provide services to Indian clients without a proper Employment or Business Visa. India currently has no dedicated “Digital Nomad Visa”.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">Understanding the Legal Grey Zone</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>India’s <strong>visa and foreign exchange frameworks</strong> were designed before remote work became common. As of 2026, there is <strong>no specific visa category for digital nomads</strong>, meaning foreigners must rely on traditional visa types such as Tourist, Business, or Entry (X) visas.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>The critical distinction is the&nbsp;<strong>source of income</strong>&nbsp;and&nbsp;<strong>nature of activity</strong>:</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Allowed:</strong>&nbsp;Working online for a foreign employer or foreign clients, with payments received outside India.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Not allowed:</strong>&nbsp;Providing services to Indian residents or companies, earning income in India, or opening a business locally without approvals.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>If a digital nomad stays within these limits — and does not engage in Indian employment — their activities generally don’t violate visa terms.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\"><strong>Which visas can digital nomads use in India?</strong></h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Digital nomads may enter India on Tourist, Business, or Entry (X) visas depending on their purpose and nationality. However, none of these explicitly permit employment in India or paid work for Indian entities.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">1.&nbsp;<strong>Tourist Visa</strong>&nbsp;– for short-term remote workers</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Designed purely for tourism and short visits.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Holders may&nbsp;<strong>work remotely for foreign employers</strong>, as long as the work doesn’t involve Indian entities.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Duration: up to&nbsp;<strong>6 months to 10 years</strong>&nbsp;(depending on nationality).</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Cannot open local offices or engage in Indian commercial activity.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Not convertible to Employment Visa from within India.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>Example:</strong><br>A British marketing consultant working online for UK clients while exploring India can stay for several months on a Tourist Visa, provided she doesn’t serve Indian clients or receive Indian income.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">2.&nbsp;<strong>Business Visa</strong>&nbsp;– for entrepreneurs managing overseas companies</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Allows participation in business meetings, investments, and exploration of opportunities.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Digital nomads managing&nbsp;<strong>foreign companies remotely</strong>&nbsp;(not Indian businesses) often use this category.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Must not draw salary or income from an Indian company.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Valid up to 5 years with multiple entries.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Requires FRRO registration for stays exceeding 180 days.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>Example:</strong><br>A Singapore-based startup founder living in Bengaluru for six months to manage his overseas operations remotely can use a Business Visa.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">3.&nbsp;<strong>Entry (X) Visa</strong>&nbsp;– for dependents or OCI holders</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Typically issued to spouses and dependents of Employment Visa holders or OCI cardholders.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Allows residence and limited activities, but not local employment.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>A good option for accompanying partners of foreigners legally employed in India.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\"><strong>What about OCI cardholders and foreign citizens of Indian origin?</strong></h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>OCI cardholders (Overseas Citizens of India) can live, invest, and work freely in India, subject to FEMA and tax regulations. They don’t require visas but must comply with income tax and reporting obligations if they earn locally.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":4} -->\n<h4 class=\"wp-block-heading\">The&nbsp;<strong>OCI scheme</strong>&nbsp;grants lifelong visa-free entry and residence rights to eligible foreign citizens of Indian origin. OCI cardholders can take up employment, start businesses, or work remotely from India — without needing a visa renewal.</h4>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>However, they are still governed by:</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Income Tax Act, 1961</strong>&nbsp;— determining tax residency and global income.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>FEMA Regulations</strong>&nbsp;— controlling foreign exchange and overseas remittances.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>RBI rules</strong>&nbsp;— governing how income can be received and repatriated.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>Exception:</strong>&nbsp;OCI holders cannot engage in restricted professions (journalism, defense research, or missionary activities) without special permission.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\"><strong>Do digital nomads have to pay Indian taxes?</strong></h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Foreigners staying in India for 182 days or more in a financial year become&nbsp;<strong>tax residents</strong>, taxable on global income. Non-residents are taxed only on income earned in India. Double taxation treaties may reduce the burden.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">Indian Tax Residency Rules Simplified</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Under&nbsp;<strong>Section 6 of the Income Tax Act</strong>, a person’s tax status depends on their physical presence:</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Non-resident:</strong>&nbsp;Stay &lt;182 days in a financial year. Taxed only on Indian-sourced income.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident (RNOR):</strong>&nbsp;Stay &gt;182 days but limited ties. Global income partly taxable.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Resident and Ordinarily Resident (ROR):</strong>&nbsp;Stay &gt;182 days in the current and previous years — global income fully taxable.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>Example:</strong><br>A Canadian software developer staying in India for 9 months while working for Canadian clients becomes a tax resident in India. Even though her clients are abroad, she may owe Indian income tax unless protected under a&nbsp;<strong>Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA)</strong>.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Digital nomads should therefore:</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Track their days in India carefully.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Maintain documentation proving income originates abroad.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Consult tax advisors for DTAA benefits (e.g., with the U.S., UK, Canada, Singapore).</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\"><strong>Can digital nomads freelance for Indian clients or register a company in India?</strong></h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>No. Foreigners without Employment or Business visas cannot legally offer freelance services to Indian clients or register local businesses. Doing so violates FEMA and visa regulations.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">Legal Position under FEMA</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>The&nbsp;<strong>Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999</strong>&nbsp;restricts foreign nationals from conducting business, consultancy, or professional activities in India without specific approval or investment through the&nbsp;<strong>FDI route</strong>.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>If a digital nomad starts offering services to Indian clients or opens local accounts to receive payment, they may be seen as establishing a&nbsp;<strong>“place of business in India”</strong>, which triggers:</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>FEMA contraventions</strong></li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Permanent establishment (PE)</strong>&nbsp;status under tax treaties</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Corporate income tax exposure</strong></li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>To work legally with Indian clients, foreigners must incorporate a company or LLP under&nbsp;<strong>Companies Act, 2013</strong>, comply with&nbsp;<strong>FDI regulations</strong>, and apply for an&nbsp;<strong>Employment or Business Visa</strong>&nbsp;accordingly.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\"><strong>Practical Compliance Checklist for Digital Nomads in India</strong></h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>✅ Use a valid visa (Tourist, Business, or Entry).<br>✅ Work only for foreign clients or employers.<br>✅ Do not receive payments from Indian sources.<br>✅ Track stay duration for tax residency (182-day rule).<br>✅ Register with FRRO for long stays.<br>✅ Maintain overseas bank accounts for income.<br>✅ Avoid misrepresentation of purpose during visa application or entry.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\"><strong>Why India has not yet introduced a “Digital Nomad Visa”</strong></h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>India’s immigration and financial frameworks prioritize&nbsp;<strong>employment-linked</strong>&nbsp;and&nbsp;<strong>investment-linked</strong>&nbsp;entries. Introducing a Digital Nomad Visa would require coordination between&nbsp;<strong>MHA</strong>,&nbsp;<strong>MEA</strong>, and&nbsp;<strong>RBI</strong>, especially regarding taxation, FEMA monitoring, and stay conditions.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>However, as remote work becomes mainstream and countries like Malaysia, Sri Lanka, and Indonesia actively attract global freelancers, India’s growing&nbsp;<strong>startup ecosystem and tourism economy</strong>&nbsp;may soon push policymakers to design a&nbsp;<strong>Digital Nomad or Remote Worker Visa</strong>.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Until then, foreign nationals must operate cautiously within the legal parameters described above.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\"><strong>FAQs for Digital Nomads in India (2026 Edition)</strong></h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>1. Can I stay in India long-term while working remotely for a foreign company?</strong><br>Yes, as long as your income comes entirely from abroad and you do not work for or earn from Indian clients. You can stay using a Tourist, Business, or Entry Visa, but must register with FRRO for stays beyond 180 days.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>2. Can I receive my freelance income in an Indian bank account?</strong><br>No, unless you are an&nbsp;<strong>OCI holder</strong>&nbsp;or have permission under FEMA. Foreign nationals should receive income in overseas accounts. Using an Indian account for local payments can be considered illegal commercial activity.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>3. What happens if I overstay my visa while working remotely?</strong><br>Overstaying is a serious violation under the&nbsp;<strong>Foreigners Act, 1946</strong>, attracting penalties or blacklisting. Always renew or exit before expiry.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>4. Will India introduce a Digital Nomad Visa soon?</strong><br>As of 2026, no formal policy exists. However, discussions within the <strong>Ministry of Tourism</strong> and <strong>MHA</strong> are ongoing. A visa category tailored for remote workers may emerge in future years.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>5. How can I avoid being taxed twice on the same income?</strong><br>If your home country has a&nbsp;<strong>DTAA</strong>&nbsp;with India, you can claim credit for taxes paid abroad. File Indian returns declaring foreign income and claim DTAA benefits using&nbsp;<strong>Form 10F</strong>&nbsp;and&nbsp;<strong>Tax Residency Certificate (TRC)</strong>.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>6. Can I rent a house or coworking space as a digital nomad?</strong><br>Yes, you can rent legally under a standard&nbsp;<strong>leave and license agreement</strong>, provided your visa allows residence. Most coworking spaces accept foreign nationals with passport and visa copies.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>7. Do I need to report my presence in India to any authority?</strong><br>If your stay exceeds 180 days, you must register with the&nbsp;<strong>Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO)</strong>&nbsp;within 14 days. For shorter stays, no registration is needed.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>8. What’s the safest visa for a long-term digital nomad lifestyle in India?</strong><br>Currently, a&nbsp;<strong>Business Visa</strong>&nbsp;offers the most flexibility for long-term stays without engaging in Indian employment, especially if you manage overseas business interests.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>9. Can couples or families move to India as digital nomads?</strong><br>Yes. The primary visa holder can enter on a Business or Tourist Visa, and dependents can enter on&nbsp;<strong>Entry (X) Visas</strong>. Children can attend international schools, but dependents cannot work locally.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>10. What about health insurance and safety requirements?</strong><br>Foreigners should maintain international health insurance covering India. Indian law doesn’t mandate local coverage, but private insurance is advisable for long stays.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">Key Takeaway</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>India welcomes foreigners who wish to live, travel, and work remotely — but the&nbsp;<strong>legal framework lags behind modern work patterns</strong>. Until a&nbsp;<strong>Digital Nomad Visa</strong>&nbsp;is introduced, foreigners can legally work online&nbsp;<strong>only for foreign clients</strong>, using valid long-stay visas and strict compliance with&nbsp;<strong>tax, FRRO, and FEMA rules</strong>.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Structuring your stay correctly from day one helps avoid visa violations, double taxation, and compliance risks — and lets you focus on what digital nomads value most: freedom and productivity.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>About the Author</strong><br>Prashant Kumar is a Company Secretary, Published Author, and Partner at Eclectic Legal, a full-service Indian law firm advising on corporate, regulatory, and transactional matters. He specialises in corporate governance, legal compliance, and brand protection, helping businesses build credible and sustainable legal foundations. He can be reached for discussions on brand strategy, compliance, and governance excellence via LinkedIn.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p></p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->",

          "content:encoded": "<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">Unlocking Equity Grants, Credit Guarantees, and Institutional Support for Farmer Producer Organisations</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>By Prashant Kumar</strong></p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\">Introduction</h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Once an FPO (Farmer Producer Organisation) is registered, the next challenge begins —&nbsp;<strong>funding and sustainability</strong>. While incorporation gives farmers a legal identity, scaling operations requires access to working capital, equity, and credit. Recognising this, the Government of India launched the&nbsp;<strong>Formation and Promotion of 10,000 FPOs Scheme</strong>, implemented through&nbsp;<strong>SFAC</strong>,&nbsp;<strong>NABARD</strong>, and&nbsp;<strong>NCDC</strong>.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>This initiative bridges the gap between policy and practice — ensuring every genuine, compliant FPO can access grants, credit, and market linkages. If you’ve already completed your incorporation process (see our guide on&nbsp;<a href=\"https://csatwork.in/how-to-register-fpo-in-india/\">how to register an FPO in India</a>), this article explains how to unlock funding through&nbsp;<strong>SFAC equity and credit schemes</strong>, and why compliance readiness is key to eligibility.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\">What is SFAC and Why It Matters for FPOs</h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>The Small Farmers’ Agribusiness Consortium (SFAC) is the national-level institution under the Ministry of Agriculture that promotes and funds Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) through equity grants, credit guarantees, and capacity-building, enabling small farmers to operate as structured, market-ready enterprises.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>SFAC plays the role of&nbsp;<strong>financial enabler and policy bridge</strong>&nbsp;— ensuring that smallholder collectives registered as Producer Companies or Cooperatives can access credit without collateral and strengthen their equity base. It partners with&nbsp;<strong>Cluster-Based Business Organisations (CBBOs)</strong>&nbsp;to train directors, review governance, and verify documentation before approving grants.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\">The “Formation and Promotion of 10,000 FPOs” Scheme</h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Launched as a five-year flagship programme, this scheme aims to create&nbsp;<strong>10,000 sustainable FPOs</strong>&nbsp;across India by mobilising farmers into producer collectives and providing them with financial and technical support. Each cluster of FPOs is assigned to a&nbsp;<strong>CBBO</strong>, which acts as a professional handholding agency.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">Key Objectives</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Organise small farmers into collective business entities.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Strengthen FPOs through capacity-building, funding, and governance support.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Facilitate&nbsp;<strong>bank linkages, institutional credit, and market access</strong>.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Create self-sustaining rural enterprises within five years of formation.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">Eligibility</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Any legally registered&nbsp;<strong>Producer Company</strong>,&nbsp;<strong>Cooperative</strong>, or&nbsp;<strong>Farmer Society</strong>&nbsp;engaged in agricultural or allied activities can apply under this scheme through the SFAC FPO Portal or via a designated CBBO.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>If you’re still setting up your FPO, read our step-by-step guide on&nbsp;<a href=\"https://csatwork.in/how-to-register-fpo-in-india/\">how to register a Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO)</a>&nbsp;before proceeding to funding.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\">SFAC Equity Grant Scheme (EGS)</h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>The SFAC Equity Grant Scheme provides matching equity support up to ₹15 lakh to strengthen an FPO’s capital base and creditworthiness, enabling it to raise higher bank finance and expand its business activities sustainably.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">Purpose</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>The equity grant doubles the FPO’s member capital, enhances its balance sheet, and increases its borrowing capacity. The grant is&nbsp;<strong>non-repayable</strong>&nbsp;and directly credited to the FPO’s bank account.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">Eligibility</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>The applicant must be a&nbsp;<strong>legally registered FPO</strong>&nbsp;(preferably a Producer Company).</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>At least&nbsp;<strong>50 active producer-members</strong>&nbsp;with valid records.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Audited financial statements for the previous year.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Properly maintained member and share registers.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">Key Benefits</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Maximum grant: ₹15 lakh per FPO (one-time).</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Matching ratio: 1:1 with member equity contribution.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Direct benefit transfer to the FPO’s account.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Monitored by CBBO and SFAC for utilisation compliance.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>For legal and compliance clarity on maintaining records post-grant, see our guide on <em>[</em><a href=\"https://csatwork.in/post-incorporation-compliance-fpos/\" data-type=\"link\" data-id=\"https://csatwork.in/post-incorporation-compliance-fpos/\">Post-Incorporation Compliance for FPOs in 202</a><em>6]</em>.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\">SFAC Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme (CGFS)</h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>SFAC’s Credit Guarantee Scheme allows FPOs to avail collateral-free loans from banks and financial institutions, with up to 85% of the loan covered under a government-backed guarantee, enabling new producer companies to access working capital and term loans without land or asset collateral.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">Highlights</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Loan amount:</strong>&nbsp;Up to ₹1 crore.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Guarantee coverage:</strong>&nbsp;75–85% of sanctioned amount.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Tenure:</strong>&nbsp;Up to five years.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Eligible lenders:</strong>&nbsp;Scheduled banks, NABARD affiliates, RRBs, and cooperative banks.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>This scheme solves the most common problem faced by early-stage FPOs — lack of collateral. It empowers Producer Companies to access loans for seed procurement, aggregation, and storage, supporting their first trading season or processing unit.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\">NABARD and NCDC Support for FPOs</h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">NABARD – Capacity and Credit Support</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Under its&nbsp;<strong>Producer Organisation Development Fund (PODF)</strong>, NABARD provides working capital, equity support, and training grants. It also funds FPO incubation and bookkeeping workshops, helping FPOs transition from informal collectives to structured agribusinesses.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">NCDC – Infrastructure and Cooperative Support</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>The&nbsp;<strong>National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC)</strong>&nbsp;focuses on infrastructure creation and long-term financing for FPOs formed as cooperatives. Typical support includes cold storage, grading units, transport facilities, and warehousing for agri-produce.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>For a comparative view, read our article on&nbsp;<em>Producer Company vs Cooperative – Which is Better for FPOs?</em></p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\">Application Process for SFAC Schemes</h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:list {\"ordered\":true} -->\n<ol class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Incorporate the FPO</strong>&nbsp;– typically as a Producer Company under the Companies Act, 2013.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Register on the SFAC Portal</strong>&nbsp;–&nbsp;<a>https://fpo.sfacindia.com</a>.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Select the Scheme Type</strong>&nbsp;– choose “Equity Grant” or “Credit Guarantee.”</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Upload Documents</strong>&nbsp;– COI, MoA, AoA, financials, member list, bank details.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Verification</strong>&nbsp;– by CBBO or State Nodal Agency.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>Grant Approval</strong>&nbsp;– SFAC transfers funds directly upon compliance clearance.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ol>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>In most cases, professional assistance from a Company Secretary or legal advisor helps streamline the process and ensures all statutory filings (like AOC-4 and MGT-7A) are up to date before submission.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\">Compliance Readiness — The Hidden Eligibility Test</h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>A common reason why FPO funding applications fail is&nbsp;<strong>non-compliance</strong>. SFAC and NABARD require evidence that the FPO is legally active and properly managed. Before applying, ensure:</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Latest ROC filings are completed.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Board meetings and AGM minutes are properly recorded.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Member and share registers are maintained.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Accounts are audited by a qualified professional.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>For a step-by-step compliance calendar, refer to our detailed guide on <em>Post-Incorporation Compliance for FPOs (2026)</em>— part of the <a href=\"https://csatwork.in/how-to-register-fpo-in-india/\">FPO Legal Series by Eclectic Legal</a>.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\">Frequently Asked Questions</h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>1. Can a newly registered FPO apply immediately for SFAC grants?</strong><br>Yes. Once incorporation and bank account setup are complete, the FPO can apply for the&nbsp;<strong>Equity Grant Scheme</strong>. However, for the Credit Guarantee Scheme, most banks require at least one year of operational history.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>2. Can an FPO avail both Equity Grant and Credit Guarantee benefits?</strong><br>Yes, both schemes are independent. An FPO can first apply for the Equity Grant to strengthen its capital and later for the Credit Guarantee to access collateral-free credit.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>3. How long does it take to receive SFAC assistance?</strong><br>On average,&nbsp;<strong>45–60 days</strong>, depending on documentation and verification speed. Delays usually occur if audited accounts or membership records are incomplete.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>4. Do private agritech startups qualify as FPOs under SFAC schemes?</strong><br>No. Only farmer-owned Producer Companies, Cooperatives, or Federations are eligible. Private companies may collaborate but cannot directly receive SFAC benefits.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>5. Is the Equity Grant refundable?</strong><br>No. It is a non-repayable government grant. However, utilisation is strictly monitored, and mismanagement can lead to withdrawal of future eligibility.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>6. Are state governments also providing top-up schemes for FPOs?</strong><br>Yes. States like Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, and Uttar Pradesh offer additional grants and subsidies for FPOs registered under the central scheme.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\">Why This Matters</h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>For any FPO, access to SFAC and NABARD funding can be a turning point. But to benefit,&nbsp;<strong>registration, governance, and compliance must go hand in hand</strong>. The most successful FPOs are those that combine legal precision with financial discipline.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Once registered and compliant, your FPO is not just a farmer collective — it becomes a recognised agribusiness capable of receiving capital, participating in e-NAM, and forming export linkages.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>For next steps, explore:</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><a href=\"https://csatwork.in/post-incorporation-compliance-fpos/\" data-type=\"link\" data-id=\"https://csatwork.in/post-incorporation-compliance-fpos/\">Post-Incorporation Compliance Checklist for FPOs (2026)</a></li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><a href=\"https://csatwork.in/fpo-taxation-accounting-india/\" data-type=\"link\" data-id=\"https://csatwork.in/fpo-taxation-accounting-india/\">FPO Taxation and Accounting Rules in India (2026)</a><br>— both part of the ongoing <strong>FPO Legal Series</strong> by Eclectic Legal.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">About the Author</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>Prashant Kumar</strong>&nbsp;is a Company Secretary, Published Author, and Partner at&nbsp;<strong>Eclectic Legal</strong>, a full-service Indian law firm advising on corporate, regulatory, and transactional matters. He specialises in&nbsp;<strong>FPO structuring, agricultural law, and corporate compliance</strong>, helping farmer groups, startups, and agri-businesses build legally sound and sustainable organisations.<br>📩&nbsp;<strong><a>prashant@eclecticlegal.com</a></strong>&nbsp;| ☎️&nbsp;<strong>+91-9821008011</strong></p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->",

          "content:encoded": "<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">What Every Farmer Producer Organisation Must Do After Registration</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p><strong>By Prashant Kumar</strong></p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\">Introduction</h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Registration gives your FPO a legal identity — but compliance keeps it alive.<br>Once incorporated under the&nbsp;<strong>Companies Act, 2013</strong>, a Farmer Producer Organisation must follow a defined set of post-registration obligations to remain legally valid, fund-ready, and credible.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>These include&nbsp;<strong>board meetings, statutory audits, ROC filings, and member record maintenance</strong>&nbsp;under the MCA’s&nbsp;<strong>V3 portal</strong>. Most importantly, timely compliance determines eligibility for&nbsp;<strong>SFAC grants</strong>,&nbsp;<strong>NABARD support</strong>, and government procurement tie-ups.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>If you’ve just completed registration (see our <a href=\"https://csatwork.in/how-to-register-fpo-in-india/\">FPO Registration Guide</a>), here’s your complete <strong>12-month compliance roadmap for 202</strong>6.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\">What Is Post-Incorporation Compliance for FPOs?</h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Post-incorporation compliance refers to all legal and regulatory tasks an FPO must complete after registration — from holding the first board meeting and appointing an auditor to filing annual returns and maintaining member records under the Companies Act, 2013 and MCA V3 portal.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\">Step-by-Step Compliance Calendar for FPOs (2026)</h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">01. First Board Meeting – within 30 days</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Hold the first meeting of directors within 30 days of incorporation.<br>Agenda should include: appointment of the first auditor, approval of bank signatories, share allotment confirmation, and adoption of the registered office address.<br>Record minutes and preserve them in the statutory minutes book.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">02. Appointment of Statutory Auditor</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Appoint a Chartered Accountant within 30 days (Form&nbsp;<strong>ADT-1</strong>&nbsp;to ROC).<br>The auditor’s report will be required for funding and annual filing purposes.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">03. Issue of Share Certificates – within 60 days</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Issue share certificates to all subscriber members. Update the&nbsp;<strong>Register of Members</strong>&nbsp;and the&nbsp;<strong>Share Allotment Register</strong>with signatures of two directors or one director and the company secretary.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">04. Maintenance of Statutory Registers</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Under&nbsp;<strong>Section 88 and 189</strong>&nbsp;of the Companies Act, an FPO must maintain:</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Register of Members and Share Transfers</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Register of Directors and KMP</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Minutes Book for Board and General Meetings</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Register of Loans, Guarantees, and Investments</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Financial and accounting records</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Keeping digital copies under MCA V3 is permitted and advisable.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">05. PAN, TAN, and Bank Account</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Ensure&nbsp;<strong>PAN and TAN</strong>&nbsp;are generated through SPICe+ or applied separately via NSDL.<br>Open a current account in the name of the FPO and deposit members’ capital.<br>Bank details are essential for availing&nbsp;<strong>SFAC Equity Grant and Credit Guarantee</strong>&nbsp;benefits (<a href=\"https://csatwork.in/sfac-fpo-funding-support-india/\">see our funding guide</a>).</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">06. GST and Other Optional Registrations</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>If the FPO trades in goods or services exceeding the prescribed threshold, apply for&nbsp;<strong>GST registration</strong>.<br>Consider&nbsp;<strong>Udyam Registration</strong>&nbsp;(for MSME benefits) and&nbsp;<strong>APEDA Registration</strong>&nbsp;(for export activities).</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">07. Annual ROC Filings – Key Forms</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Every Producer Company must file:</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>AOC-4:</strong>&nbsp;Financial Statements (within 60 days of AGM)</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>MGT-7A:</strong>&nbsp;Annual Return (within 60 days of AGM)</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>DIR-3 KYC:</strong>&nbsp;Annual Director KYC (by 30 September)</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li><strong>ADT-1:</strong>&nbsp;Auditor appointment (within 15 days of AGM or Board meeting)</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>File via&nbsp;<strong>MCA V3 portal</strong>&nbsp;using your FPO’s digital signature and director DINs.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">08. Annual General Meeting (AGM)</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Hold the&nbsp;<strong>first AGM</strong>&nbsp;within nine months of closing the first financial year; thereafter within six months each year.<br>AGM agenda includes:</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Approval of financial statements</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Appointment of auditor and directors</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Approval of member patronage bonus or surplus distribution</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Maintain attendance records and signed minutes for inspection readiness.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">09. Accounting, Audit &amp; Recordkeeping</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Maintain books of account as per&nbsp;<strong>Section 128</strong>&nbsp;of the Companies Act: cash book, ledger, journal, and member-wise transaction record.<br>Audit annually through the appointed CA. Audited accounts are mandatory for SFAC, NABARD, and cooperative funding eligibility.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading {\"level\":3} -->\n<h3 class=\"wp-block-heading\">10. Taxation &amp; Regulatory Filings</h3>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Even if agricultural income is largely exempt, FPOs must file <strong>ITR-6</strong> annually.<br>Segregate agricultural and non-agricultural income clearly.<br>Refer to our article <em>[</em><a href=\"https://csatwork.in/fpo-taxation-accounting-india/\" data-type=\"link\" data-id=\"https://csatwork.in/fpo-taxation-accounting-india/\">FPO Taxation and Accounting Rules in India (2026)</a><em>]</em> for a deeper explanation.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\">Governance Best Practices for Producer Companies</h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Conduct at least&nbsp;<strong>four board meetings per year</strong>, spaced 90 days apart.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Circulate meeting notices at least seven days in advance.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Record attendance, quorum, and resolutions accurately.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Display transparency in member transactions and patronage distribution.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Governance quality directly impacts investor and grantor trust.<br>Our next article on <em>FPO Governance and Management Structure (2026)</em> explores these responsibilities in detail.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\">Common Mistakes That Trigger Non-Compliance Notices</h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:list -->\n<ul class=\"wp-block-list\"><!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Missing the first Board Meeting deadline.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Failing to issue share certificates within 60 days.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Late filing of AOC-4 and MGT-7A.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Inaccurate member records or lack of updated registers.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item -->\n\n<!-- wp:list-item -->\n<li>Using personal bank accounts for FPO transactions.</li>\n<!-- /wp:list-item --></ul>\n<!-- /wp:list -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>Such lapses can attract penalties and restrict access to institutional grants.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:separator -->\n<hr class=\"wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity\"/>\n<!-- /wp:separator -->\n\n<!-- wp:heading -->\n<h2 class=\"wp-block-heading\">Why Compliance Matters for Funding and Credibility</h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>A compliant FPO is automatically&nbsp;<strong>eligible for SFAC, NABARD, and NCDC support</strong>, as these agencies verify ROC filings and audit reports before sanctioning any financial aid.<br>Compliance is not just paperwork — it’s the proof of governance, transparency, and readiness to grow.</p>\n<!-- /wp:paragraph -->\n\n<!-- wp:paragraph -->\n<p>For funding guidance, visit&nbsp;<a
